hotham.narrative: After a warm and very blustery night, the temperature has dropped and the wind has backed off a notch but is still a strong northerly.  The current temp is minus 1.5, heading for a top of 1 degree, there is high cloud in the sky, and we may see a snow shower or two during the day.  Due to the warm evening followed by rapid cooling in the last couple of hours, the snow is firm and slick out there this morning, but it should soften somewhat during the day.  It'll be a good morning for arcing turns on the groomers, but I'd avoid anything off-piste until there has been significant softening.  There'll hopefully be more significant softening with the top-up of snow expected over the next couple of days.  Stay tuned! Lifts are scheduled to open at 8.30 today but check the lift status before heading to your preferred option.  Sharpen those edges and feel the carve! Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: After a warm and very blustery night, the temperature has dropped and the wind has backed off a notch but is still a strong northerly.  The current temp is minus 1.5, heading for a top of 1 degree, there is high cloud in the sky, and we may see a snow shower or two during the day.  Due to the warm evening followed by rapid cooling in the last couple of hours, the snow is firm and slick out there this morning, but it should soften somewhat during the day.  It'll be a good morning for arcing turns on the groomers, but I'd avoid anything off-piste until there has been significant softening.  There'll hopefully be more significant softening with the top-up of snow expected over the next couple of days.  Stay tuned! Lifts are scheduled to open at 8.30 today but check the lift status before heading to your preferred option.  Sharpen those edges and feel the carve! Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: We've had 4 cm of cold dry snow overnight and it is still snowing lightly this morning.  The current temp is minus 3.6, the wind is a moderate northerly, and we are heading for a top of minus 2 degrees.  The snowguns have had another good run and are still pumping it out right now.  The base is rock solid and there are a few centimeters of dry snow sitting on top.  The groomers will be the best option, but you may find a few drifted areas offering some shallow fresh turns.  Hunt around and you'll find the fun, but beware of steeper off-piste zones that will still be very slick underneath.  The forecast is calling for snow showers to continue today and tomorrow, and there are signs of very significant promise in the near future.   Stay tuned! Rug up for the windchill and have a good one out there.   Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: There has been a nice little refresh over the last couple of days. This morning we've got a further 7cms of new snow to add to yesterday's tally, bringing the total to 11cms so far from this system. At 6am it's still snowing lightly which is forecast to continue on and off throughout the day. The current temp is -2.5, headed for a top of -1 degrees and the wind is light to moderate from the NW. At the moment the snow feels reasonably dry underfoot and should make for some really fun turns with the best of it being had early before there's any temperature rise. The groomers will be in great shape from the outset, perfect for arcing some turns. Off piste is a little more tricky to read. I reckon some areas will have accumulated enough snow for some smooth turns, however, you might still be feeling the hard base underneath on ridge tops and some of the steeper terrain so be sure to feel it out before diving in. There are signs of significant promise beginning to show in the long range forecast and next week could be very interesting. Stay tuned to see how this develops over the coming days..... Have a great day out there! Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: I was surprised to see it snowing lightly walking across the carpark early this morning. While not a lot, it's added up to a fresh 2 centimetres and mixed in with some overnight snowmaking there should be some fun to be had out there today. The current temp is -1.9, headed for a top of 2 degrees and right now there's a moderate WNW wind with stronger gusts at times. There's still the odd fine flake in the air and a light fog in the Village. The texture on the groomers feels great underfoot and I reckon they'll be the best option first up on a very edgeable surface. With the cool temps off piste will likely be firm and probably best avoided until some softening occurs. For the early birds the Road Runner Quad will be spinning from 7:30am for WRX First Tracks. In more good news the Pirate Life Rail Jam is on tonight down at the Big D. Kicking off at 5:30pm, get along and check out all the action under lights! Rug up for the windchill and have a great day. Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: It looks like a glorious day on the way.  The sky is clear, the snow guns are blazing and there is just a puff of a breeze from the north.  The overnight low was minus 5.8, the current temp is minus 4.8 and we are heading for a very pleasant top of 4 degrees.   The snow has firmed up a little since yesterday but the groomers I kicked on the way to the office have some nice dry texture on top.  It should be a good morning for carving turns on the piste, and some of the off-piste zones should be riding well too.  The sunny aspects should soften further as the day warms.   Get out there and make the most of the easy conditions today, as it looks like things are going to get real tomorrow. Stay tuned!  Road Runner will be spinning at 7.30am for First Tracks this morning.   And get along to support our incredible Volunteer Ski Patrol at the Big Gig fundraising auction tonight.  The General at 8.30pm.   Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: We have some weather coming folks.  Some high cloud has moved in, and the wind has picked up to a stiff northerly, which is meant to get increase significantly as the day progresses.  There is no precipitation at the moment, but there is a big blob moving our way on the radar. The current temp is minus 1, so hopefully the initial precip falls as snow and then we'll see what happens later on when the day warms.  Regardless, the temperature is forecast to plummet overnight, and heavy snow is predicted during the early hours, so we should wake to a much whiter mountain tomorrow morning. The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before softening with precip of any type.   Get out there for the early turns.... or brave the elements when things get real later on.  Road Runner is scheduled for 7:30 First Tracks.    Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: It was a warm and wild night on the mountain, but the temperature dropped at about 4 am and we've picked up 4 cm of snow since then and it's still snowing pretty well as I write.  The current temp is minus 2, which is forecast to get a little colder through the day, and the wind is a strong northerly. Although there has not been too much snow just yet, it should be skiing and riding really well, with drier snow sitting on top of a soft and wet base underneath.  Snow showers are predicted to continue in bursts, so conditions should keep improving as the day progresses.    Rug up for the wind chill and get out there for a few fresh turns.

hotham.narrative: It should be a pretty good day on the hill.  Not quite the 50-year storm, but we picked up another 13 cm during the day yesterday and we should see more snow later today and tomorrow.   The sky is clear to the east and cloud is moving in from the west.  The current temperature is minus 1.6, heading for a top of minus 1, and the wind is a moderate westerly. The slight warming late yesterday, followed by the cooling in the last few hours has stiffened the snow surface, but there should still be really good turns to be had out there.  The groomers will be in good shape and there'll be fun to be had off-piste as well....just watch out for the very thin crust in places. The wind has backed off enough that I think all scheduled lifts should be right to go this morning.  Get out there and get into it. Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: It started snowing again last night and we've accumulated 4cms on the stakes so far with more pulses showing on the radar this morning. After an overnight low of -3.3, the current temp is -1.9 and we're headed for a top of -1 degrees. I reckon the weather station has frozen up, but right now it feels like a moderate to strong northwesterly. It's still snowing lightly as I type and there's a light fog in the Village. The texture on the groomers feels great underfoot and they'll be offering plenty of fun turns from the outset. There may have been enough new snow off piste for some shallow smooth turns in certain areas. Hunt around some of the more sheltered terrain and see what you can find. If you're up for it, night skiing is scheduled this evening down at the Big D from 5pm to 8pm under the lights! Rug up for the windchill and have a great day out there. Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: Anything could happen this morning. Right now, there's an alpenglow out to the east with cloud moving in from the west and the forecast is calling for a cloudy day with the chance of a snow shower.   At 6am it's -2 degrees which was also the overnight low as we head for a top of +2 degrees. The wind has swung around and is currently moderate from the WSW. With yesterday's warming followed by a cooling the snow has definitely firmed up overnight. The groomers will be the go first up this morning and it feels like there's enough texture to get your edges in. Off piste will likely be very challenging with some areas having formed a crust so be sure to feel it out and perhaps wait for any softening to occur. In other news, pending weather and final checks the Drift T-Bar is scheduled to spin at some stage today. Keep an eye on the App and the lift report for all the latest updates. Have a great day out there. Cheers, Burner.

The wind has swung around and is currently moderate from the WSW. With yesterday's warming followed by a cooling the 4cm of fresh snow that fell yesterday has definitely firmed up overnight. The groomers will be the go first up this morning and it feels like there's enough texture to get your edges in. Off piste will likely be very challenging with some areas having formed a crust so be sure to feel it out and perhaps wait for any softening to occur. In other news, pending weather and final checks the Drift T-Bar is scheduled to spin at some stage today. Keep an eye on the App and the lift report for all the latest updates. Have a great day out there. Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: It looks as though we're in for a ripper Friday in the mountains. The sky is filled with stars, there's an alpenglow out to the east and it won't be long before the sun makes an appearance. The current temp is +0.1, headed for a very pleasant top of 5 degrees and right now there's a moderate wind from the SW. Even though it's not super cold, the snow has had a freeze and will start out firm before softening later on. It sure was great to get the Drift up and running yesterday and there'll be more fun turns to be had out there today. Start off on the groomers before moving around to your preferred off piste options as the day warms. Road Runner will be spinning from 7:30am for WRX First Tracks which is also where the ANC Series is taking place. Stop by the track and check out all the action where some of the world's best Snowboard Cross and Ski Cross athletes will be racing, including our very own Olympic gold medallist Josie Baff. Best of luck to all the competitors. Slap on the sunscreen and have a ripper day. Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: It looks like a glorious rinse and repeat of yesterday, with just an added touch of cooling breeze.  The sky is clear, the current temperature is right on zero, heading for a top of 7 degrees and there's a light to moderate northerly breeze which is predicted to drop right off during the morning.   The snow has had another decent freeze overnight, so it will be firm this morning and will soften on the sunny slopes as the day warms. The groomers should be good for carving turns first up, and some off piste zones will come into shape as the day progresses.   Road Runner will be spinning for First Tracks from 7:30am. Slap on the screen and follow the sun for fun turns all day.   Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: Yet another magic day on the mountain coming up.   The sky is clear and there is just a puff of a breeze from the southeast.  The current temp is right on zero and we are heading for a balmy top of 7 degrees.  The snow has had another good freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before the sunny aspects soften for fun spring-like turns.  There should be good turns to be had on the groomers from the get-go, and some off-piste areas will be worth a look once the day warms.  Just beware of shaded and south facing slopes that may stay slick for the day.   Slap on the screen and follow the sun for fun turns all day! Cheers Bill

perisher.narrative: Fresh snow and more on the way!. Fresh snow has landed at Perisher! We received a dusting of 3cm overnight, with more forecast to fall throughout the day. Check the Snow Stake to see for yourself! It's currently -2 degrees in Perisher Valley, with a top of 1 degrees expected, so rug up if you're heading up the mountain today. Expect cloudy skies again, scattered snow showers, and westerly winds of 25 to 35km/h. Our snowmakers made the most of the cool overnight temperatures, firing up 194 guns from 5:35pm and still running at time of writing, giving Mother Nature a hand topping up the base. Meanwhile, the grooming team have prepared 42 runs with fresh cord, ready for you to carve up. 36 lifts are expected to spin today, though strong winds may affect operations. Keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop. Check back tomorrow to see how much more snow falls today and tonight!

perisher.narrative: 5cm fresh snow and still snowing!. We had another 5cm of snow recorded on the snow stake overnight, and it's still snowing this morning! The flakes are forecast to continue throughout the day, and we should see another few centimetres by the end of the day. It's currently -1.7 degrees in Perisher Valley and the wind is a westerly 20 km/h. We have a forecast top of 1 degrees with the windchill making it feel colder, so layer up before heading out. Visibility is fairly impaired this morning with low cloud hanging around the mountains, so stick to the trees and use a low light lens. perisher.narrative: Another 10cm of fresh snow! . It was snowing heavily as the resort closed yesterday and we had another 10cm of snow overnight , bringing the total for the week to 18cm. Winter might have been a little late this year, but it's well and truly arrived with the start of August. It's currently a chilly -3 degrees in Perisher Valley and the wind is blowing from the southwest at around 15-20km/h. We're headed for a top of 3 degrees. This morning's fog is lifting as I write this and the forecast is calling for a partly cloudy day, so it should clear up and visibility will be fine. There isn't any more snow forecast today and we should be in for a couple of clear days before the next front rolls in. Speaking of the next front, that looks to be the big one, with the Weatherzone forecast calling for between 47cm and 95cm of snow from Sunday through to Thursday next week. The snow guns were also firing overnight to add to the natural snowfall. We have 38 lifts scheduled to run and 55 groomed runs across the resort, and the skiing and riding will be awesome. With the fresh snow, we may have additional lifts come online over the coming days, so download the Perisher App to be the first to know, and keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates. It will be a great day out there, so get out and enjoy it!

perisher.narrative: Three resort areas interlinked!. Happy Friday and good morning from Perisher! We have some high cloud about this morning and the chance of a snow flurry, but the forecast is calling for a mostly sunny day. Conditions are expected to clear as the day wears on. It's currently -1 degrees in Perisher Valley with a forecast top of 4 degrees. The wind is blowing from the west at around 20km/h and should stay that way for most of the day. 178 snow guns ran from 4:30pm yesterday until about midnight, when the relative humidity rose. The great news is we have 41 lifts scheduled to run today, with Interceptor opening yesterday and Sun Valley and Freedom Quad scheduled for today. Plus, three resort areas connected , with skiing between Perisher Valley, Blue Cow and Guthega now on offer. You can ski from Perisher to Smiggins via Piper T-Bar, but you'll need to take the free Guest Shuttle to return to Perisher Valley. With 62 runs groomed across the resort, it's going to be a great day out there, with plenty of room to explore. perisher.narrative: Sunny Saturday: the calm before the storm!. We're kicking off the weekend with a mostly sunny day, a top of 7 degrees, and west to north-westerly winds around 13km/h. It's shaping up to be a great day on the mountain! It's a chilly start this morning at Perisher, with the temperature currently sitting at -8 degrees. Those cool overnight conditions meant our snowmaking team could fire up the snow guns, with 188 running across the resort from 5:30pm and still going this morning. Thanks to fresh snowfall earlier in the week and good snowmaking conditions, the Mountain Operations team has been able to open more lifts and terrain, including the recently opened Interceptor Quad Chair, Freedom Quad Chair and Sun Valley T-Bar. There are also now three interconnected resort areas , so you can ski and ride between Perisher Valley, Blue Cow and Guthega. With 41 lifts expected to spin and 64 groomed runs on offer today, there's plenty of space to discover your moment on the mountain. Please note: you can ski from Perisher to Smiggins via Piper T-Bar, but you'll need to take the free Guest Shuttle to get back to Perisher Valley. Blue Cow Cup races continue today on Front Valley, best of luck to all the junior racers! Elsewhere across the resort, you'll find live music at Jax Bar, Mid-Station and Blue Cow, so be sure to check it out between laps. Make the most of today's fine weather, as wintery conditions are set to roll in tomorrow , and fingers crossed, more snow with it!

perisher.narrative: Sunny Saturday: the calm before the storm!. We're kicking off the weekend with a mostly sunny day, a top of 7 degrees, and west to north-westerly winds around 13km/h. It's shaping up to be a great day on the mountain! It's a chilly start this morning at Perisher, with the temperature currently sitting at -8 degrees. Thanks to fresh snowfall earlier in the week and good snowmaking conditions, the Mountain Operations team has been able to open more lifts and terrain, including the recently opened Interceptor Quad Chair, Freedom Quad Chair and Sun Valley T-Bar. There are also now three interconnected resort areas , so you can ski and ride between Perisher Valley, Blue Cow and Guthega. With 41 lifts expected to spin and 64 groomed runs on offer today, there's plenty of space to discover your moment on the mountain. Please note: you can ski from Perisher to Smiggins via Piper T-Bar, but you'll need to take the free Guest Shuttle to get back to Perisher Valley. Blue Cow Cup races continue today on Front Valley, best of luck to all the junior racers! Elsewhere across the resort, you'll find live music at Jax Bar, Mid-Station and Blue Cow, so be sure to check it out between laps. Make the most of today's fine weather, as wintery conditions are set to roll in tomorrow , and fingers crossed, more snow with it!

perisher.narrative: Wild winter weather ahead. Perisher is set for some wild winter weather today! It's currently 1 degrees, and while this morning brings a mix of sun and cloud, conditions will turn as the day progresses, with high cloud and wind moving in. We suggest making the most of the morning! Blizzard-like conditions are due to roll in this afternoon, bringing rain that should hopefully fall as snow at the peaks. Today's top will be 4 degrees, with north-westerly winds of 30 to 45 km/h and stronger gusts here and there. High wind may impact lift operations, so check the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop! 41 lifts scheduled to spin today and 64 groomed runs to carve up. Conditions on the slopes will be hard packed with some man-made snow on top, as the snow guns have been running since around 9pm last night and are still going this morning. With cloud cover rolling in, visibility on the slopes could be affected, so please take care while skiing and boarding. In between runs, catch some live music from the Greg Nunan Duo at Jax Bar and the Steve Edmonds Band at Blue Cow Bistro! We should start reaping the benefits of this storm tomorrow, with rain turning to snow showers overnight and continuing through the day! The days following are also looking promising for snowfall , so stay tuned to see how much we get.

We're headed for a top of 1 degrees and there's a high chance the snow showers will continue throughout the day. Winds are forecast to be westerly 35 to 50 km/h. 41 lifts are set to spin today, though keep an eye on the lift report as the winds may impact some lift operations. The Perisher App will also keep you posted with real-time updates. We have 53 runs groomed across the resort and Blue Cow, Perisher and Guthega are all still interlinked, offering plenty of space. This should be the last stormy day before conditions start to clear up as we head towards the weekend.

perisher.narrative: Another 5cm and a clear day ahead. We had another 5cm of fresh snow overnight and are in for some clearer days ahead now that the storm has rolled through. The forecast is calling for a partly cloudy day, but the sky is clear this morning and you can't spot any of those clouds! It's currently hovering just below 0 degrees and we're headed for a top of 4 degrees. With the variable conditions of the past few days, we've lost a couple of lifts: Piper and Burke T-Bars in Smiggins have closed for now. We still have 39 lifts set to spin and 58 groomed runs across the resort, giving you plenty of room to explore. Around the resort today, we have live music at Blue Cow Bistro from 1pm and at Jax Bar from 12pm. For our park riders, please note that the Front Valley park will be light on features today (and maybe tomorrow) as we rebuild for Val's Blue Steel Rail Jam presented by Oakley this Sunday, an event not to miss. Looking ahead, we're building to a big weekend of live music and events, with Red Bull Sessions, Subaru Scavenger Hunts, and our Sunrise Sessions at Blue Cow kicking off tomorrow morning (quick, there's only a couple of spots left). With great weather on the forecast, it's a weekend not to miss.

perisher.narrative: Kickstarting the weekend with a bluebird!. We're waking up to a chilly -5 degrees at Perisher this morning, with clear skies overhead. Today is shaping up to be mostly sunny with a top of 7 degrees and very little wind, making for a great day on the mountain. The snowmaking team made the most of the cold overnight temperatures, firing the guns from 7:00pm last night right through to this morning. On the slopes, expect firm, fast conditions underfoot with a fresh layer of man-made snow on top. With 40 lifts spinning and 62 groomed runs to explore, there's plenty of room to roam this sunny Saturday. There's also live music dotted around the resort: catch Car Kills Kiwi at Blue Cow, DJ Bolta at Mid-Station, and the Greg Nunan Duo and Vibe Band at Jax Bar. Red Bull Sessions are also on today, bringing together passionate skiers and boarders for a day of riding, progression and good times alongside Australia's best Red Bull snow athletes, including Olympian Valentino Guseli. The Red Bull DJ Cat will be spinning tunes live from the top of Front Valley Park! The Subaru Wilderness Scavenger Hunt is also underway. Four flags are hidden across the resort, and finding one wins you a Subaru Wilderness Prize Pack. Clues will be shared throughout the morning on social media, so follow @perisher_resort and @subaruaustralia on Instagram to track them down! We also want to with good luck to everyone racing in the Perisher Masters today! Please note, racing will take place on Front Valley. Have a great weekend on the slopes!

perisher.narrative: Sunny Sunday Laps and Val’s Blue Steel Rail Rumble!. The weekend sunshine continues, with today forecast to be mostly sunny with occasional cloud, a top of 8 degrees, and light north-westerly to north-easterly winds. It's currently -4 degrees in Perisher, and the snow guns fired up around 11:30pm last night with some still going this morning. Expect conditions to be firm and fast underfoot, with hard-packed snow base. 40 lifts are set to spin again today, and with 61 groomed runs freshly prepped, it's shaping up to be a great one for Sunday laps. On the slopes, the Perisher Masters races continue on Front Valley this morning, while park riders have their own big day ahead with Val's Blue Steel Rail Rumble taking over the Front Valley Park. Some of Perisher's best will be throwing down for a shot at Oakley, XTM and Hydroflask gear, plus some serious cash prizes, with the Red Bull DJ Cat on hand to keep the energy up. Head to Front Valley to catch the action. There's plenty more music around the mountain too, with Car Kills Kiwi playing Jax Bar and Vibe Band bringing the tunes to Blue Cow Bistro! Have a great Sunday!

latest.narrative: A mostly sunny Monday at Perisher. Happy Monday from Perisher! It's currently clear skies and -3 degrees, with today forecast to bring mostly sunny conditions, a top of 7 degrees, and northeasterly winds up to 17km/h. 38 lifts are scheduled to spin today, and the grooming team have prepared 57 runs across the resort for you to explore. Expect firm, fast conditions underfoot on hard-packed snow, which will likely soften as the day goes on. Perisher would like to extend a warm welcome to all guests competing in the State Interschools this week. Best of luck with your races! To our other guests, please note that most Interschools races will be taking place on Front Valley and Centre Valley, so it's a great time to explore our other resort areas. Have a great day out there!

latest.narrative: Yet another magic day on the mountain coming up.   The sky is clear and there is just a puff of a breeze from the southeast.  The current temp is right on zero and we are heading for a balmy top of 7 degrees.  The snow has had another good freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before the sunny aspects soften for fun spring-like turns.  There should be good turns to be had on the groomers from the get-go, and some off-piste areas will be worth a look once the day warms.  Just beware of shaded and south facing slopes that may stay slick for the day.   Slap on the screen and follow the sun for fun turns all day! Cheers Bill

August is a big month on the mountain, with a packed calendar of on-snow events, races and activities, alongside plenty to enjoy off the slopes. From exciting action on the snow and Nordic trails to live music, food, family activities and events across the village, there’s something happening throughout the month.
